sentences: MoltenVK reports `fragmentShaderBarycentric` but can't create a pipeline with the row above's inputs: its SPIR-V to MSL conversion stops with "PerVertexKHR decoration is not supported in MSL" (MoltenVK 1.4.2 on an Apple A18 Pro and, reported by @DomasUrbonas in #166, an M4 Pro), so `ps_interp_f16_high` failed on every Mac.

With the flag no `PerVertexKHR` (and, for these reads, no `BaryCoordKHR`) is used: every VS `exp paramN`, mesh param and `--mesh-compute` vertex (`tools/mesh_compute_vs.py`) also exports the channel's two f16 halves decoded to f32 (`UnpackHalf2x16`), low halves at location 29 − 2N and high halves at 30 − 2N, below MoltenVK's 31 locations (124 components); a PS `*_f16` read of attrN.c takes component c of that ordinary smooth input, then p2 clamps and narrows as before.

With the flag no `PerVertexKHR` (and, for these reads, no `BaryCoordKHR`) is used: every VS `exp paramN`, mesh param and `--mesh-compute` vertex (`tools/mesh_compute_vs.py`) also exports the channel's two f16 halves decoded to f32 (`UnpackHalf2x16`), low halves at location 28 − 2N and high halves at 29 − 2N, so nothing goes above location 29: MoltenVK's `maxVertexOutputComponents` is 124 because Metal counts `gl_Position` in its 128 vertex-output scalars, and the Khronos validation layer counts it too, so a VS output at location 30 failed VUID-RuntimeSpirv-Location-06272 on `vs_ids` (SHADER-291); a PS `*_f16` read of attrN.c takes component c of that ordinary smooth input, then p2 clamps and narrows as before.

Interpolation is linear, so the device interpolating the decoded halves gives the same P0 + i(P1 − P0) + j(P2 − P0) as the per-vertex path, with the interpolator's rounding instead of explicit f32 arithmetic. f32 and `v_interp_mov_f32` reads of such a location are the raw word as on any location (flat = the provoking vertex's word, exact).

A producer leaves out the halves of a param whose locations would land on one of its own params (params 0..P−1 leave room for the halves of params 0..(29 − P) / 2), and a PS whose decoded-half location is also an attribute it reads is rejected (`Unsupported`), not mislinked.

The index records `f16_halves` ({param: [low, high location]}) on both sides; a pipeline links when the PS's entries are among its producer's.

Chosen like the wave64 mode: `tools/vk_subgroup_info.py` reports `per_vertex_inputs` (false without `fragmentShaderBarycentric` or on driver ID MoltenVK), and `make_game.py` and `run_gpu_tests.py` turn the flag on where it is false (`LEONIDA_F16_INTERP_FALLBACK=1`/`0` overrides the runner; `build.py` takes only the variable, since it may run in WSL).

Without the flag the translation is unchanged: all 139 GPU-test modules are byte-identical to main's, with and without `--bary-fallback` and with `--mesh-compute --wave64-emulate`, so NVIDIA and AMD keep the exact per-vertex path.

Confirmed on an Apple A18 Pro (macOS 26.6.2, MoltenVK 1.4.2): `ps_interp_f16_high` drawn with `vs_f16_pack` passes natively and with wave64 emulation, every one of its 4,096 pixels bit-exact to f16 of the exact u and v in both halves (it failed before at pipeline creation), and `ms_f16_pack` through `--mesh-compute` (`LEONIDA_MESH_COMPUTE=1`) passes too; `tests/semantic/test_f16_interp_fallback.py` checks the PS reads (1.75 and 9.0 from the decoded halves), the VS exports (one-lane interpreter), the overlap rules and the default being unchanged.

**Unverified:** a PS whose producer exports more params than leave room for the halves it reads (it reads that producer's param, not halves: the `f16_halves` entries then don't match); devices with fewer than 31 output locations.
CPU check (TEST-398, `FallbackStagePair`): with ordinary VS exports at 28 and 29, the PS reads those values (5 and 7 in the test) in place of attr0's decoded halves (2 and 3).
Only the PS lists attr0 in `f16_halves`.
With param28 as the last export, location 28 carries its ordinary value and location 29 has no VS output.
When the last ordinary export is at 27, both stages list the pair and the PS reads 2 and 3.

The move from 30 to 29 (SHADER-291) was checked on an Apple M5 (macOS 27.2.1, MoltenVK 1.4.2, Khronos validation layer 1.4.363): over the 170 GPU-test modules `vk_pipeline_check` reported VUID-RuntimeSpirv-Location-06272 on 6 vertex shaders at location 30 and on none at 29; the same 15 modules list `f16_halves` for the same params, `run_gpu_tests.py` gives the same result per test, and `ps_interp_f16_high` reads back byte-identical pixels.

Checked by `tests/semantic/test_f16_interp_fallback.py`, `tests/semantic/test_interp_p1lv_f16.py`, `tests/test_mesh_compute_vs.py`, `runtime/test/shader_library_test.cpp`, `runtime/test/spirv_f16_halves_test.cpp`, and `runtime/test/d3d12_f16_halves_test.cpp` (real Vulkan 1.3 draw on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Ti, driver 32.0.16.1088, Windows 11: 16-param VS + colliding PS both synthesized and relocated render exact RGBA `(64, 191, 127, 255)`).
